root_motivation: A freshly signed-up tenant's tools/list dumps the entire host.*/billing.* control-plane surface at once -- dozens of tools with no ordering, so a young agent has no signal for what to call next. This PRD narrows the anonymous (pre-signup) tools/list to a 12-tool starter set, keeps the full listing for every authenticated/bound session, emits notifications/tools/list_changed when a session binds so a client's cached list doesn't go stale, and has every host.* result for a tenant under 5 distinct tools used carry a next: {tool, why} hint from a static table -- suppressed once a tenant is past that threshold, header-authenticated, or has opted out via host.agent.profile_set(hints: false).
user_persona: A freshly signed-up agent calling mcphost for the first time, and the operator who wants that agent to discover tool_call/tool_share/table.create organically instead of reading the whole control-plane surface up front.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given an anonymous (pre-signup) session, When it calls tools/list, Then it receives exactly the 12-tool starter set (signup first, then host.quickstart, host.redeem, billing.plans, host.whoami, host.tool_publish, host.tool_call, host.tool_test, host.state.set, host.state.get, host.state.list, host.tool_share), not the full control-plane surface.

Given an authenticated session (bearer header) or a session bound by signup/host.redeem, When it calls tools/list, Then it receives the full, unchanged listing -- the starter-set narrowing applies only to anonymous sessions.

Given a session that calls signup (or host.redeem) and binds, When the bind completes, Then the server emits notifications/tools/list_changed on that connection (capabilities.tools.listChanged advertised in get_info) and the session's next tools/list returns the full listing.
Given a new tenant with zero host.* tools used, When host.tool_publish succeeds, Then the result carries next: {tool: "host.tool_call", why: <=120 chars} and no other entry.
Given a tenant that has used five distinct host.* tools, When any further host.* call succeeds, Then no next field is present.
Given host.agent.profile_set(hints: false), When any later host.* call succeeds, Then no next field is present, regardless of distinct-tool count.

Given a header-authenticated (Authorization: Bearer) session on a new tenant, When host.tool_publish succeeds, Then no next field is present -- hints apply only to tenant_key-argument or session-bound callers.
Live/production: a real young tenant on https://mcphost.dev/mcp sees a next hint on its first host.tool_publish after ship.
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned; AC8 is the Live/production-only requirement and needs operator authorization this coding sandbox does not have. See the coder dispatch's own deferred list.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given seven days in which 10 hints were shown and 3 were followed, When host.usage is called, Then hints.shown_7d == 10 and hints.followed_7d == 3, independent of the response's own window/by argument.

scope: src/handler.rs: starter_tools()/STARTER_TOOL_NAMES (AC1), list_tools's Auth::Anonymous branch and its new session-binding resolution step (AC2/AC3), get_info's enable_tool_list_changed() (AC3), bind_session_to_created_tenant's peer.notify_tool_list_changed() call (AC3), maybe_attach_next_hint (AC4-7), host.agent.profile_set's new hints schema property (AC6).
src/control.rs: next_hint_for()/NEXT_HINT_TABLE/NEXT_HINT_DEFAULT (AC4-7), usage()'s new hints: {shown_7d, followed_7d} field (AC9).

src/db.rs: migration 0059 (host_tool_usage table, hint_events table, agent_profiles.hints column), count_distinct_host_tools_used/host_tool_already_used/record_host_tool_use/record_hint_shown/resolve_pending_hint/hints_usage/insert_hint_event_for_test, AgentProfileRow.hints field, set_agent_profile's new hints parameter.
src/agents.rs: profile_set's hints argument parsing and echo.
contracts/host-tools.v1.json: regenerated for host.agent.profile_set's new hints schema property.

src/oauthclient.rs, src/compat_check.rs, tests/common/mod.rs, examples/*/proof.sh, examples/docs-qa/docs-qa.sh: SSE-response-unwrapping fixes, made necessary by AC3's notify_tool_list_changed() upgrading mcphost's stateless POST responses to text/event-stream whenever a bind fires (an inherent rmcp behavior, not a bug) -- every caller that previously assumed a plain application/json response to signup/host.redeem (and, transitively, anything that calls through src/oauthclient.rs::call_tool or src/compat_check.rs::rpc_call) needed to handle the SSE-wrapped form too.
non_goals: Hiding tools from authenticated sessions -- Non-goals: the starter-set narrowing applies only to anonymous, pre-signup sessions; every authenticated or session-bound caller keeps seeing the full listing, unchanged.
Building a recommender -- Non-goals: next is chosen from one static, hand-written table keyed by the tool just called, not a model or ranking of the tenant's actual usage pattern.
Changing host.quickstart's try_before_call table -- Non-goals: that table is a separate, already-shipped discovery mechanism this PRD leaves untouched.

Implicit signup auto-binding a session without a signup/host.redeem call -- that is a separate, not-yet-built PRD; AC3's notify_tool_list_changed() fires only on signup/host.redeem's own successful bind.

additional.test_file_names_use_test_prefix_nexttool: test_prefix nexttool (the PRD's own frontmatter field): tests/nexttool_ac<NN>_<slug>.rs, same convention as every other test file in this repo.
additional.ac8_deferred_operator_provisioned: AC8 is a Live acceptance criterion (a real young tenant on https://mcphost.dev/mcp after ship) -- deferred, not built or tested here; a build agent never provisions, deploys to, or authorizes changes on a live/prod host.
additional.distinct_tools_used_is_a_new_table_not_t: The PRD's own technical considerations suggested deriving the distinct-tools-used counter from the pre-existing calls table ("no new table"). Deviated from this: calls only logs a tenant's own published-tool invocations (local tool names), never control-plane verb calls like host.tool_publish/host.whoami themselves, so "already used host.tool_call" could never be true against it, and widening calls' population to include every host.* verb call risked breaking many existing host.usage call-count assertions across the suite. A dedicated host_tool_usage table is the safer, more isolated design given real suite-stability constraints.
additional.sse_upgrade_on_every_bind_is_inherent_no: The PRD's own technical considerations note ("when the client has none open, the notification is dropped and the full list appears on the client's next tools/list anyway") undersells the actual rmcp behavior: a stateless POST response is upgraded from application/json to text/event-stream whenever the handler emits ANY notification before its final response, which happens on every single signup/host.redeem bind (mcphost's stateless transport mints a fresh, always-unbound session id per request when the client doesn't echo Mcp-Session-Id, so the very first bind always fires). This is architecturally correct and unavoidable -- confirmed by reading rmcp's stateless_sse_response source -- not a defect to route around; every caller of signup/host.redeem across this repo's own tests, oauthclient.rs, compat_check.rs, and examples/*/proof.sh needed an SSE-aware body parse instead.
additional.hints_9_field_is_a_fixed_seven_day_windo: AC9's own example ("Given seven days in which 10 hints were shown...") pins hints.shown_7d/followed_7d to a constant 7*24*3600-second lookback computed fresh on every call, independent of host.usage's own window/by argument -- not a reuse of the request's own window parameter.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does maybe_attach_next_hint record_host_tool_use AFTER the distinct-tool-count eligibility check rather than before?
five_whys_trace.a: AC4 requires "zero tools used" to reflect tenant state strictly BEFORE the current call; recording the current call's own tool first would inflate the pre-call count by one and could flip a should-get-a-hint call into a past-the-cutoff one, breaking the AC4/AC5 boundary exactly at the cutoff.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is header-authenticated-ness computed as !via_tenant_key_arg rather than a new, independently-tracked flag?
five_whys_trace.a: call_tool already tracks via_tenant_key_arg/via_session_binding for auth-precedence; a header-authenticated call is precisely the one that used neither tenant_key argument nor session binding to resolve its tenant, so reusing the existing flag avoids a second, parallel source of truth for the same fact.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the next hint table key off the tool that was JUST called rather than the tenant's whole usage history?
five_whys_trace.a: Non-goals explicitly rules out building a recommender; a static table keyed by "what did you just do" is the simplest mechanism that still produces a contextually relevant suggestion (publish -> call, call -> share) without any ranking logic or historical analysis.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is host_tool_already_used checked before attaching a hint, rather than always suggesting the table's fixed next tool?
five_whys_trace.a: Suggesting a tool the tenant has already used would be a stale, useless hint (e.g. re-suggesting host.tool_share after the tenant already shared); checking already-used status keeps every hint pointing at something genuinely new to that tenant, falling through to NEXT_HINT_DEFAULT (host.quickstart) when the table's own suggestion has already been exhausted.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does AC2's test only exercise header-authenticated and session-bound (post-signup) listings, not the /u/<secret>/mcp URL-bound path the PRD's own AC2 text mentions?
five_whys_trace.a: /u/<secret>/mcp belongs to PRD-mcphost-url-bound-tenants, a separate, independently-shipped PRD not in this dispatch's scope -- AC2's own wording covers "authenticated/bound sessions" generically, and the two auth paths this repo's handler actually resolves for an authenticated tenant (bearer header, session binding) are both exercised; a third path this repo doesn't own cannot be tested here.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does the distinct-tools-used counter derive from the existing calls table, per the PRD's own technical-considerations suggestion?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- see hard_constraints.additional.distinct_tools_used_is_a_new_table_not_the_existing_calls_table. A dedicated host_tool_usage table is used instead, a deliberate, documented deviation from the PRD's own suggestion.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does notify_tool_list_changed() firing on every bind break any existing test that assumes a plain JSON response from signup/host.redeem?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes, extensively -- see hard_constraints.additional.sse_upgrade_on_every_bind_is_inherent_not_a_bug. Every affected call site (tests, src/oauthclient.rs, src/compat_check.rs, examples/*/proof.sh) was given SSE-aware response parsing rather than suppressing the notification.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is host.usage's hints field windowed the same as the rest of the response (the window/by argument), or fixed?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Fixed at 7 days always -- see hard_constraints.additional.hints_9_field_is_a_fixed_seven_day_window, per AC9's own literal example.
